correctness.rationale: The effective time A increases at unit speed and jumps to its value at the sampled past time. Its distribution is input-independent, giving a random-unitary CPTP map at every fixed time. For the coherence f the jump compensator gives f'=−(r+iω)f+(r/t)∫₀ᵗf(s)ds with f(0)=1; its regular solution has the stated Kummer parameters. The chosen state difference has eigenvalues ±|f|, so its trace distance is |f|. An independent exact rational reproduction verified 17/10000<|S₃|²<18/10000 and 119/10000<|S₄|²<120/10000 for the 80-term sums, with the claimed margins beyond the 1/20 and 1/10 thresholds. The tail bound follows from |a|<1, |z|<11 and the ratio bound 11/81 after the first omitted term; the verified bound is below 10⁻¹⁰. The strict revival contradicts trace-distance contractivity under positive trace-preserving maps, without requiring invertibility. Since 0≤rA_(u/r)≤u, the change in the two endpoint moduli across ratios is at most 7|Δh|, leaving >3/200 throughout the band. Any pair of eigenstates with the given gap isolates the same coherence, regardless of other levels. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/5096d329-af1e-4b98-bc22-b92a792f594c/recheck_witness.py. The supplied check_backflow_exact.py was inspected, not executed. This is a sufficient spectral band, not a classification of all ratios or a computation of the optimized backflow measure.

value.rationale: The main result is an operational counterexample, not a reevaluation of a special function for its own sake. It distinguishes a constant positive physical event rate and CPTP snapshots from positive divisibility, with a finite robustness margin against changing the gap. The uniform statement makes the witness usable in a multilevel Hamiltonian without checking its full spectrum or solving any intermediate map.
